**Netflix Terms of Use Summary:**

The **Netflix Terms of Use** outline the rules and agreements between you and Netflix, the streaming service provider. 

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services described on Netflix's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Netflix can use your content (like ratings and comments) to improve and train their AI systems, as long as it's in line with your settings and the law.
* **Household Sharing:** You'll need to pay for any additional members in your household, beyond the primary account holder. A clear definition of what constitutes a 'Netflix Household' is provided.
* **Billing and Cancellation:** The rules for changing your payment method or canceling your account have been updated.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Any disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court), with class-action waivers. You can opt out of arbitration within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, but the terms describe the conditions for doing so.
* **Contact Info:** If you have questions, check Netflix's published legal contact information.

**Concerns for Users:**

* The **Dispute Resolution** clause may be unfavorable to users, as it requires binding arbitration with class-action waivers, which means you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit if Netflix is accused of wrongdoing.
* The **Termination** clause means either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

The service is called the Disney+ Subscriber Agreement. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**1. What are these Terms for?**
These Terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+, which means they apply to the products and services provided by Disney+.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Streaming titles may show ads even on 'no ads' tiers:** This means that even if you pay for a service with no ads, you might still see ads on some streaming titles. This change took effect in January 2025 for new subscribers and March 2025 for existing ones.
* **User-submitted content is used to train AI/ML systems:** When you submit content on Disney+, it may be used to make the service better and improve the AI/ML systems (computer learning systems). This will happen subject to your settings and applicable law (which is not specified here).
* **Binding Arbitration with a 30-day opt-out:** If there's a dispute, you'll need to go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. This means you won't be able to join a group lawsuit against Disney+. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but it's not clear if this applies to existing accounts.
* **Termination:** Disney+ or you can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these Terms, see Disney+'s published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Class-action waiver in Arbitration:** This means you won't be able to join a group lawsuit against Disney+, which may limit your ability to hold the company accountable for wrongdoing.
* **Limited control over user-submitted content:** The Terms don't specify exactly how your content will be used, subject to your settings and applicable law. This may give Disney+ more flexibility to use your content without your consent.
* **No clear opt-out for arbitration in existing accounts:** It's not clear if existing subscribers can opt out of binding arbitration, which may limit their rights in case of a dispute.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**PayPal User Agreement Summary**

The PayPal User Agreement governs your relationship with PayPal when using their services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Service Name**: PayPal User Agreement

**Relationship**:
These Terms of Service apply to the products and services listed on PayPal's official terms page (clause 1). This means that the agreement affects not only the primary PayPal services but also other services offered by the company.

**Content and Usage**:
PayPal collects user-submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems (clause 3). However, this use of content is subject to your settings and applicable law.

**Dispute Resolution**:
Most of these Terms of Service require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers (clause 5). This means that:

* You can't join a class-action lawsuit with others who have had similar problems.
* Any disputes will be resolved in a private process with a third party, rather than in court.

**Note**: This exception only applies if you have created a new PayPal account within 30 days of making this agreement. If this applies to you, you have a 30-day opt-out window to decline binding arbitration.

**Termination**:
Either PayPal or you can terminate the agreement according to the conditions outlined in the Terms of Service (clause 6).

**Harmful Clauses**:
- Mandatory binding arbitration may make it more difficult and expensive to resolve disputes.
- Class-action waivers limit the likelihood of being part of a larger lawsuit and can reduce the ability to get a broader settlement.

Take note that this is a summary, and it's essential to review the full Terms of Service document, especially before agreeing to them.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Name:** eBay User Agreement

**Summary:** This contract between you (the user) and eBay outlines the terms and conditions of using eBay's services, including how user-submitted content is used, how disputes are resolved, and how personal data is collected and processed.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services offered by eBay, as described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** eBay uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. The terms describe how this is done, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The user's personal data is collected and processed in accordance with eBay's published Privacy Policy. You can find more information about this policy elsewhere.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for this are described in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, see eBay's published legal contact information.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This means that if you have a dispute with eBay, it will be resolved through a private process instead of in court. This clause may be harmful to users if it prevents them from seeking justice through the court system.
* **Class-action Waivers:** The arbitration process may also bar you from participating in class-action lawsuits, making it harder to hold eBay accountable for collective grievances.
* **30-day Opt-out Window:** The time limit for opting out of arbitration may be too short for some users, particularly those who may not be aware of the clause or need more time to understand it.
* **Control over User Data:** The terms allow eBay to use and distribute user-submitted content as they see fit, subject to your settings and applicable law. However, this may not provide sufficient transparency or control for users.

Please note that these provisions and red flags are based on the provided text and are intended to provide general information. If you are concerned about specific aspects of the eBay User Agreement, it is recommended that you review the document in full or consult with a qualified attorney.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

These are the Amazon Conditions of Use, which cover your relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Amazon, they can use it to improve their services, including their AI/ML systems, without getting your explicit permission.
* **Privacy**: Amazon does not disclose how they collect and process your personal data, but their published Privacy Policy sets out the categories of data they collect.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You and Amazon will use binding arbitration instead of going to court, and there's no class-action lawsuits (meaning you won't be able to represent a group of people with similar concerns).
	+ Note: Steam, a service owned by Valve, has removed mandatory arbitration, which might be a concern for users who want to pursue a class-action lawsuit.
* **Termination**: Either you or Amazon can terminate the agreement at any time, depending on the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about the terms, you should look at Amazon's published legal contact information.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* The Terms of Service don't outline how Amazon collects and processes your personal data explicitly, which might raise concerns about confidentiality and data ownership.
* The provision on content and license allows Amazon to use your contributed content without permission, which might make users uncomfortable, especially if they created original work.
* The binding arbitration clause might be seen as limiting users' options to resolve disputes, and the absence of class-action lawsuits might dissuade users from seeking justice.

Please note that this summary only covers the **2024** version of the Amazon Conditions of Use.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Amazon to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 .

response:
The service is called Apple Media Services, and these Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with Apple and its related services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **How the Terms Apply**: These Terms apply to Apple Media Services, which includes products and services listed on Apple's official terms page. 

* **What the TOS Means for Your Content**: Any content you submit to Apple, such as images, emails, or other data, may be used by Apple to improve and train its artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems. Apple will use your data according to your settings and applicable laws.

* **Privacy**: Your personal data is collected and processed according to Apple's Privacy Policy. Please refer to the Privacy Policy for details on what data is collected and how it is used.

**Dispute Resolution**: 
- Most terms require you to resolve disputes through private binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means that you and Apple will not go to court to resolve disputes, but rather work through a neutral third-party mediator.
- There is an optional 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Other Key Points:**
- Apple may terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions described in the live document (you can find this at the link provided in the Terms).
- For questions or concerns about the Terms, please visit Apple's published legal contact information.

**Red Flags:**

* **Use of User Content for AI/ML**: Apple may use and modify your submitted content for AI and ML training and improvement. This might be a concern for users who are concerned about data privacy and anonymity. Please note that Apple will use your data according to your settings and applicable laws.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

These are the Terms of Service for the iCloud service from Apple. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**1. What you're agreeing to**: These terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to various Apple products and services.

**2. Key uses and changes**: The updated terms mention:
- Advanced Data Protection (Secure encryption),
- References to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, 
- How stored content might be used for legal or safety reasons.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: When you upload content, Apple can use it to improve its services and train its AI/ML systems, as per your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: The Privacy Policy, linked from the Terms, explains personal data collection and processing.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You'll have to use binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process outside of court, and you'll waive your right to join a class-action lawsuit. This applies to most users, but Steam (Valve) has already removed this requirement (Note: this is specific to the company Steam, not a feature of the iCloud service).
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can terminate the agreement under the outlined conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions, see Apple's contact information.

**Clauses of concern**:

* Binding arbitration may present challenges for users in resolving disputes with Apple privately and with limited public oversight.
* Class-action waivers and binding arbitration may discourage other users from filing complaints.
* It is unclear how often Apple will review stored content and access it under the stated conditions.
 
Please note that these concerns are identified within the Terms of Service and may not represent a full analysis or the perspectives of others.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** The Terms of Service apply to Snapchat (or "Snap").

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Snap when you use their products and services.
* When you submit content on Snapchat, like pictures, videos, or messages, you're granting Snap a license to use and adapt this content to improve their AI and ML systems, as long as it's in line with your account settings and applicable law.
* The Terms reference the company's published **Privacy Policy**, which explains what kind of personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* If a dispute arises, you and Snap will try to resolve it through **binding arbitration** (a private process instead of court). You have 30 days to opt out of arbitration when creating a new account.

**Provisions that might raise concerns:**

* **Data Sharing:** Snap may share your data with parents through Family Center if you're under 18. You might want to review their Privacy Policy if you're concerned about this.
* **Arbitration:** Some users might find mandatory arbitration clauses limiting, as they can prevent lawsuits and class-action lawsuits. However, this is a broad industry practice and Snap has included an opt-out period.

**Red flags do not necessarily mean 'be alarmist' about a company's intentions. A 'red flag' is just a reminder of a term you might want to review.** The Terms of Service do not explicitly address important aspects like location or age restrictions for features, but you can assume the usual age restrictions apply.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

The service name is Pinterest, and these Terms of Service outline the company's rules and guidelines for users.

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with Pinterest and cover the products and services described on their official terms page.

**Content and License:** When you share content on Pinterest, you agree that the company can use it to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems, as long as your account settings allow it and applicable law permits.

**Privacy:** Pinterest's published **Privacy Policy** outlines how they collect and process personal data. (We won't elaborate on the policy here, but you can find it at policy.pinterest.com.)

**Arbitration:** Most of the updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account.

**Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions listed in the live document.

**Key Provisions to Consider:**

* **Giving Pinterest permission to use your content:** Be aware that by using Pinterest, you're consenting to having your user-submitted content used by the company for various purposes (see Content and License section).
* **Binding arbitration:** This clause may limit your ability to file class-action lawsuits against Pinterest in the future. You may want to review this provision carefully before deciding whether to opt-out of arbitration.
* **Termination clause:** Understand that either party can terminate the agreement, so be aware of your responsibilities and rights under this provision.

Overall, these terms aim to govern your interactions with Pinterest and ensure that both parties understand their roles and responsibilities.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

The Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with Tumblr, a platform for sharing thoughts, ideas, and multimedia content.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These TOS govern your use of Tumblr's products and services, including what you can and cannot do on the platform.
* **Content and License:** By sharing content on Tumblr, you grant the company permission to use and modify your submissions for its own purposes, like operating and improving the platform, and potentially training artificial intelligence (AI) systems. However, you can control how your content is shared outside of Tumblr by setting your visibility settings.
* **Privacy:** Tumblr will collect and process your personal data, which is overseen by the company's published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a problem arises, you're required to resolve disputes via binding arbitration, which means a private process instead of going to court. This includes waiving your right to pursue class-action lawsuits. However, this only applies if you don't opt out within the first 30 days of creating an account (Steam users are exempt from this requirement).
* **Termination:** Either you or Tumblr can terminate the agreement, subject to any applicable conditions.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Use of AI and ML Systems:** The company may use your public content for AI training without your permission, unless you opt out. Be aware that this clause may raise concerns about how your data is used and the potential implications.
* **Limited Choice in Dispute Resolution:** The mandatory arbitration clause limits your options for resolving disputes, potentially making it harder to seek redress.
* **Termination on Either Side:** You're not provided with a clear explanation of what might trigger termination or how to appeal a termination decision.

**Platform Name:** The new, updated Tumblr Terms of Service are in effect as of 2024 and replace the 2023 version.

While the Terms of Service provide important context for your use of Tumblr, be aware of these key aspects and how they might impact your experience on the platform.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Dropbox Terms of Service (Effective 2024)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the agreement between Dropbox and users of Dropbox's products and services. Key provisions include content use, data processing, dispute resolution, and account termination.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms of Service apply to Dropbox's products and services as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Dropbox uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems, subject to user settings and applicable law. This means that the content users upload to Dropbox may be used to train AI models, but only with their consent.
* **Privacy:** The Terms of Service reference Dropbox's published Privacy Policy, which explains the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means that if a dispute arises, users may have to resolve it privately with Dropbox, without the option to join a class-action lawsuit. However, users with Steam accounts have an exception from mandatory arbitration. Users must opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either Dropbox or the user may terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses to Users:**

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This may leave users with limited options for resolving disputes and may prevent them from joining a class-action lawsuit. However, users with Steam accounts are exempt from this provision.
* **Use of User-Submitted Content:** While Dropbox states that user consent is required to train third-party AI models, the Terms of Service do not provide explicit details on the safeguards in place to protect user data.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Canva Terms of Use: A Summary**

This version is effective as of 2024, replacing the 2023 version.

**Key Provisions:**

The Terms of Service for Canva govern your relationship with the company and apply to its products and services.

**Ownership and Content:**

* You retain ownership of the content you submit to Canva.
* Canva can use your submissions to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, but only subject to your settings and applicable law.

**Dispute Resolution:**

* If you and Canva disagree, most cases will require you to use binding arbitration instead of going to court.
* This means a private dispute process (binding arbitration) instead of a public court hearing.
* A 30-day opt-out window applies to new accounts for this requirement.

**Termination:**

* Either you or Canva can terminate the agreement if the conditions outlined in the document are met.

**Other Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service cross-reference Canva's published Privacy Policy.
* Canva may terminate the agreement if the user breaches these terms, among others.
* For questions, see the published legal contact information at the TOS URL.

**Potential User Risks:**

The updated terms include new rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio), which raises concerns:

* **Ownership of AI outputs:** Canva owns rights to the outputs from its AI tools, subject to certain restrictions.
* **Training other AI models:** You are restricted from using Canva-generated content to train other AI models.

Please be aware of these changes, especially if you plan to use Canva's AI tools.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name: Figma Terms of Service**

The Figma Terms of Service is a contract between you (the user) and Figma that outlines the rules and guidelines for using their products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Figma uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (such as "Make Designs" and "Visual Search"). This happens subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Figma's Privacy Policy (linked in these terms) explains how they collect and process personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Figma requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, you can opt-out of this within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Use of user content:** Figma may use your submitted content to train their AI/ML systems, even without explicit permission. However, this is only done subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Arbitration clause:** The forced arbitration and class-action waiver may make it difficult for users to resolve disputes or join a class-action lawsuit.

It's essential to carefully review the Figma Privacy Policy and understand how it relates to these terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

response:
**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service

**Summary:** These terms outline the relationship between you (the user) and Stack Overflow, governing how you use the platform and what happens with your submitted content.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Stack Overflow products and services (listed on the company's terms page).
* **Content and License:** When you submit content (e.g., questions and answers), you grant a license to Stack Overflow to use it for their operations, improvements, and AI/ML training, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Stack Overflow's **published Privacy Policy**, which explains how personal data is collected and handled.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The updated terms require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you can't pursue a lawsuit against Stack Overflow, and any disputes will be resolved through a private process. This provision may harm users who feel they cannot access justice.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, visit the company's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The required binding arbitration may limit users' access to justice.
* **Generative AI / LLM restriction:** Stack Overflow may limit or extract submitted content for AI training without permission if a commercial agreement isn't in place.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

The Terms of Service apply to Quora's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms govern your relationship with Quora.
* **Content and License**: Quora may use your user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. 
* **Privacy**: The Terms cross-reference Quora's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of disputes, you may have to resolve them through binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of court, without the option to join a group lawsuit (class-action waiver). You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement.
* **Contact**: For questions, see Quora's published contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Intellectual Property Rights**: Quora may use your content to improve its AI/ML systems, which could potentially infringe on your intellectual property rights.
* **Data Storage**: As Quora's business grows, you don't have much control over your data, which may be stored on its servers.
* **Arbitration Clauses**: You may be required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which can limit your options for seeking redress in case of a dispute.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

These are the Terms of Service for using 23andMe's products and services.

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service govern your relationship with 23andMe and apply to any products or services you use from the company.
* You agree to bind any disputes to arbitration instead of going to court (see binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)).
* You have a 30-day window to opt out of arbitration, but if you don't write to 23andMe to opt out, you consent to arbitration.
* Class-action lawsuits are limited (a class-action lawsuit is a lawsuit brought on behalf of a group of people with similar claims).
* If you don't provide notice of a dispute within the specified timeframe (30 days), any potential claim will be waived.
* 23andMe can terminate the agreement with or without reason (termination of contract), as described in the document.
* The company's Privacy Policy (a separate document that explains how personal data is collected and used) is referenced, but not detailed within these Terms.

**Clauses May be Harmful to the User:**

* Mandatory arbitration: This clause may make it difficult for users to seek justice in court if they feel 23andMe has wronged them.
* Class-action lawsuit limitations: This change may reduce users' ability to join a group lawsuit against 23andMe if they have similar claims.
* Shortened dispute-notice window: If you don't provide notice of a dispute within 30 days, you may lose the chance to seek compensation.

Please note that these are the provisions as stated in the document and are not necessarily intended to provide a recommendation or suggestion.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name and Terms Overview:** Twitch is a streaming service governed by these Terms of Service. The updated version, effective in 2024, includes new rules for Branded Content disclosure, expanded user content licensing for clips, replays, and AI-generated highlights, and updated dispute-resolution procedures.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and Licensing** (Section 3): Twitch uses your submitted content to improve the service and develop AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.

* **Termination** (Section 6): Either party can end the agreement under specified conditions.
* **Contact** (Section 7): For questions about these terms, visit the company's legal contact information.

**Clauses of Concern:**

* **Dispute Resolution with Binding Arbitration**: This can limit users' options for resolving disputes with Twitch. If you don't agree to binding arbitration, you must opt out within 30 days of creating a new account. Please review the details in Section 5 carefully.
* **Limited User Control Over Content**: While you control your submitted content settings, Twitch may use them to operate and improve the service without explicit permission. Review Section 3 for details.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use (which governs your relationship with Roblox)

**Key Provisions:**

**1. Scope:** These updated terms apply to you (the user) and Roblox, specifically the products and services listed on Roblox's official website.

**2. Content and License:** You grant Roblox a license to use your user-submitted content (like game creations) to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.

**3. Privacy:** Roblox's published Privacy Policy outlines what personal data they collect and how they process it. The terms also allow Roblox to use your data for their AI/ML systems as per your settings and applicable law.

**4. Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Roblox, both parties must go through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, which means you can choose not to use this process initially.

**5. Termination:** Either you or Roblox can end the agreement, but the terms outline specific conditions for this.

**6. Contact:** If you have questions, check out Roblox's official legal contact information.

Regarding **harmful clauses:**

* **Class-action waivers**: If you go through arbitration, you may not be able to join a larger group lawsuit against Roblox. This might limit your ability to hold them accountable for collective issues.
* **Arbitration requirement**: You must use binding arbitration, which might be inconvenient or expensive if you're not familiar with the process.
* **Data usage for AI/ML**: While your settings and applicable law apply, it's essential to review and understand how Roblox uses your data (and potentially shares it with AI/ML systems).

Keep in mind that these Terms of Service are a standard part of the agreement when using Roblox's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: The terms apply to your use of Epic Games' products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you create content, like user-submitted content, Epic Games can use it to improve and train their AI/ML systems, as long as your settings permit. However, the terms don't clarify how long Epic Games retains your content.

* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, Steam (Valve) is an exception and no longer requires arbitration. Note that class-action waivers are also in place, meaning users can't join a collective lawsuit against Epic Games.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms don't specify the conditions for termination.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, visit Epic Games' published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers**: This means that users can't take Epic Games to court and can't join a collective lawsuit against the company.
* **Unclear Data Retention Policy**: The terms don't specify how long Epic Games retains user-submitted content, which might be concerning for users who value data protection.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Summary of the DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service**

These Terms of Service apply to your relationship with DoorDash, an online food delivery and ordering service. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms govern your use of DoorDash's products and services.
* **Content:** When you submit content (e.g., ratings, reviews, photos), DoorDash may use it to improve and train its AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms link to DoorDash's Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data DoorDash collects and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration, with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either you or DoorDash can terminate the agreement as specified in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This means you can't join or participate in class-action lawsuits against DoorDash. This can limit your ability to seek collective relief for similar claims.

**Important Contact Info:** If you have questions about these Terms, check the company's published legal contact information at https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service. 

**Additional Tips:**

* Make sure to review the specific product or service terms linked to on the company's official terms page, as they may have additional rules and requirements.
* Be aware of how your submitted content might be used by DoorDash, and adjust your settings accordingly.
* If you're not comfortable with the arbitration and class-action waiver provisions, consider speaking with a legal advisor.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

**Service Name:** Uber US Terms of Use (effective 2024)

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Uber and apply to their products and services. Here's a walk-through of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms cover your use of Uber's products and services, as described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you use Uber, you agree to let the company use your content (including ratings and reviews) to improve and train their AI and machine learning systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Uber's Privacy Policy explains what personal data they collect and how they process it. However, the Policy is a separate document from these Terms of Service.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Uber, you'll need to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). Most contracts have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but be aware that classes can not proceed if there's binding arbitration.
* **Termination:** Either you or Uber can terminate the agreement under specific conditions, as described in the live document.

Some provisions that may be of concern to users:

* ** Binding arbitration:** Users will need to resolve disputes through private arbitration, which can be expensive and may limit their options if they disagree with the outcome.
* **Class-action waivers:** Due to the binding arbitration clause, users may also be restricted from joining or participating in class actions, which can limit their ability to hold Uber accountable for group-wide issues.
* **Use of user content:** While user-submitted content is used to improve Uber's services, there's no clear explanation of what happens to the data or what protections are in place to safeguard user rights.

Please note that users should review the full Terms of Service document and consult the Privacy Policy for a more comprehensive understanding of their relationship with Uber.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .

**Service Overview**: These terms govern the relationship between Airbnb and users of its products and services.

**Key Provisions**:
* **Scope**: These terms apply to all products and services listed on Airbnb's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Airbnb uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, in accordance with user settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Personal data is collected and processed under Airbnb's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of data collected and how it's used.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with class-action waivers. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions, which are outlined in the live document.

**Notes on Provisional Concerns**:

* **Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers**: Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) may leave users with limited options in resolving disputes, and waiving class-actions might prevent users from taking collective action against Airbnb.
* **AI/ML Systems**: While Airbnb uses user-submitted content to train AI/ML systems, it's unclear how this may impact users' personal data or whether users have any control over data used for training these systems.

**Flagged Clauses**:

* **Dispute Resolution**: Binding arbitration with class-action waivers might be seen as limiting users' options and collective action.
* **Termination**: While termination is a standard practice, the specific conditions outlined in the live document seem unclear and might leave users at risk.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AIRBNB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Airbnb and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new AnyWhere/Icons experience terms, revised cancellation and refund policies (including AirCover updates), added language on automated/AI-driven listing detection (e.g. anti-party tools), and updated arbitration provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Airbnb to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 .
